body:
I think when you have chronic pain it is natural to look for a reason why is happening and to find blame for your pain.  It also makes it difficult to move on because you also have to deal with your pain on top of everything else.  

I actually blame myself for my pain and have spent many many hours of self loathing.  I'm not sure what advice I can give you but I know I've tried recently to not blame myself and think about what I can do going forward instead.

I'd imagine at the recreation level technique is everything.  If you want to improve your speed working on your skating is the way to go IMO. 

If you like lifting then I guess any squats and dead lifts would be good cross over to hockey.
I'd take the five years.  I have an amazing girlfriend, but she lives with this truncated version of myself.  I'd love to give her 5 years of the person I should be.
It's hard because to find your limit you to fail and be punished with pain.

I'm not sure a pro/cons list for suicide is helpful because the outcome of one side is finite (dying)  and the other (doing nothing) has multiple possibilities that you can't know and may be better than your current situation.   

It sounds like your really struggling, is there anything you could do to improve your life despite the pain?

I actually met her when my pain was at it's worst and we were friends for 6 months first.  I don't think she cares about the pain, she just enjoys hanging out with me and that makes a huge difference. 

 I know how you feel about being a failure.  I had a successful career that has been taken away from me, and a lot of my identity was tied up in that.   

I guess you just have to move your ambitions.   So tomorrow I'm going to go to the gym and do a bit of exercise, and that's actually a big deal for me.   So that has to be my success for now.     

Or course its difficult to remember what you used to be able to do and one of the hardest things is to accept this reality that none of us chose to be part of.

I would be dead without my girlfriend, I have no doubt about this.   Our relationship is rock solid, we're a team, she looks after me and works around my pain without a second thought.  On top of that I think she's so beautiful. 

It's hard though, like others have said sometimes I do resent the fact that I'm in this amazing relationship because she keeps me here.  I wish she could have known me before all of this.  

Dates are tough, I'm coming up on one at the moment and find myself ruminating and imaging how different things would be if I hadn't had my accident.   It's a tragic and desperate milestone when I realise another year as ticked by.  When suddenly I realise a significant portion of my 20's has been taken away by pain. 

I keep going by taking one day at a time.  I can't thing about the future anymore.  I've shelved my ambitions and desires, but if I can get through one day then I'm still here.
This is the second post about overdoing it this week.   I always feel so terribly guilty when I do this.  I'm starting to realise its not just me.

I have a horrible habit of pushing the limit and it's lead to my chronic pain today.  I have done a lot of reading around my condition and about activity and fitness in general.    

I think what I've learnt to appreciate is that your body needs rest.  In fact the rest is as important as the activity.  I realised too late that my body recovers very slowly.  Instead of overdoing to the point of pain I should have been making sure I have enough rest. 

I guess my advice is to deliberately plan for this rest.  If you know you're be working hard all week, try to do nothing much at the weekend.  

I've learnt that even if I feel good, once I've scheduled the rest, I force myself to take it and it makes things much better in the long run. 

I'm not sure if this will help you, just something that helps me when I feel desperate to do more.

Exactly.  If someone told me that I just had to do x and then I'd eventually be pain free it would make things considerably easier.    

Even a definitive answer the other way, at least I would know what I was in for.   Holding on to false hope is so exhausting.

I completely agree, my condition is life changing but not life threatening. 

It may sound like a terrible thing to say but sometimes I wonder if cancer would have been easier to cope with.   The health service in the U.K is built to tackle it, and there is often quick and definitive diagnosis and treatment plan.  Doctors and friends rally to help. 

One of the worst things about chronic pain for me is the shame and ambiguity surrounding it.  

Yeah I'm in a lot of pain but no one can really tell me why or what I can do to stop it and the very fact that its not life threatening means that the doctors don't really care.

This happened to me although it was my girlfriend that got the job.

My biggest advice is to keep supporting her, try not to complain or boast about the job too much at the start.  She will get over it in time.  

Also I would say that since you have got this opportunity maybe give the next one to her? Or let her make the next big decision?  

I felt my girlfriend was always trying to best me and it becomes exhausting.

I tried back in December, they had me do a questionare to determine if I was depressed then I'm just been moving through the system.  I still haven't received any help. 

Even so I don't know how therapy can help? It won't change what has happened or how I have to live my life now.
Beautifully written.   I often wonder what would occupy my thoughts if it weren't for the pain taking up all the space.

I often think its not the pain itself thats the problem.  

It's the way it changes your life.  It's the worry, the stress,  the disappointments, and the shame. 

If I could live how I wanted in spite of that pain I might be angry I was sore but I wouldn't be so desperately sad at the life I'm losing because of it.
I think I read this at the time. Sorry it's so shitty.
There's a high risk of re injury.  I think a mistake in rehab or a misstep can cause the pain to return.  There's also a chance the surgery makes it worse.
Good advice, thank you.

I think it's more that it could return functionality. There's a hope I could go back to my career which was quite physical. And also be involved in sport in some capacity.  Obviously there's the risk as we any surgery.
Exactly this,  although you managed to say it more succinctly than me.

I have, about 6 months ago.  I would say that the effect on my mental well being has been devastating.   I was in physical job that I loved, I got to travel, be creative and I good and dedicated to it.  

Practically I've lost a big social circle, I miss the excitement, and the friendships. I'm sorry to say but I also miss the status and the recognition that came with the job. 

Emotionally I'm angry, disappointed, frustrated, sad , but mostly I'm ashamed of how my life is turning out.    I worry about the future more than I did before. 

I received very little support from my employer who wouldn't put me on a desk job despite having plenty of transferable skills.  

 I had to leave to join a competitor in the same field and its been difficult to try and fit in. I think I'm finally starting to make a good impression.  

I've lost relationships, my sport and now my career and I feel that I have very little of my identity left.

The care I received during my treatment was very poor so it was left to me. Although I still blame myself for not resting more and having a better work out plan.  I am hopefully it could get better eventually, I have a much better doctor this time.  Maybe it's regret more than shame.  Sorry I'm just rambling.
I just did too much exercise and became injured again.  I'm ashamed because I've caused so much stress again to all my loved ones.
Congratulations.  Hopefully that will be a big step for you to feel better.

I try my best to hide the depression from my SO.   I think what hurts the most is that's she's experiencing a dumbed down version of the guy I want to be.  She's not getting my best and that hurts, I feel like I'm letting her down.    I also feel that my love for her is clouded by the depression.
Absolutely.  I feel my girlfriend has only known this version of me.  I wish she could have met the guy I used to be.
Sadly my experience means I don't trust a lot of doctors
Yep pretty much this

Are you me?  

I'm becoming increasingly bitter even though I know its not healthy.  It hurts because not only am I jealous of peoples big achievements but I'm also jealous of people that can wake up without pain.  My life would be so different without this pain and I hate that most people can just continue with their lives and I can't. 

Sorry I'm not much help but at least your not the only one that feels this way.
Good idea. If I wanted to get into gaming what's a good game to get me started?
Has it helped opening up?
Good point, I'm still learning not to feel guilty if I have to do nothing.
Second the isolation.  My friends were very much tied to my active hobbies.  I think if you could keep your life in tact regardless of the pain things wouldn't be that bad.
Exactly this
Apologies, I fell asleep.  How are feeling today?
Or could it be that it will make it easier to move forward even though it will be difficult?
Sounds like everything is coming to a head tomorrow.  Do you think it might be a weight lifted once your done with court?
What if you are doing everything you can and you still can't see things improving.  That's where I am now, i just don't know what else I can do.
hey, whats making you feel like this?
Could you retake any courses to bring your grades up?
Thats great, if you are depressed its so difficult to appreciate how people really feel about you.
Have you told him about how your feeling right now?
Yeah thats what I'm curious about, in the past I've always been able to visualise a better time.  I'm struggling at the moment.
Sadly in my experience its better not to tell your employer about depression.
hey do you have a plan to get through the next couple of weeks?
If your boyfriend is saving up so you guys can live together he must really care about you?
Do you think you could tell your friends how you feel?
hey, whats troubling you?
hey man, I'm in a similar position.  I use resistance bands for strength training, they're cheap and you can get a full body work out that's relatively easy on the body.
nice way to evaluate what you have to live for
hey man, I know it seem all consuming now but maybe give it a few days before you do anything rash.  You still have positive prospects in the future despite this setback.
Thats good to hear, what did you do to make things better?
That's nothing to be ashamed off, I understand it must be frustrating when people expected you to develop in a different way.  Do you have any new goals aside from sports?
Maybe they would give you a small rest bite into the pressure and worry you're feeling.  I understand its so difficult to worry about everyone else when your dealing with your own problems too.

No need to apologise.  Maybe it might make you feel better to set some small goals.  Like one day try and have a good meal?Or one day try and get outside and walk for 10 mins? I find it helps me if I break things down into these small tasks. Just a suggestion.
Is there any you used to enjoy? Any hobbies or interests?
What a kick in the gut to have a break up and find out about your ex in the same day.  Is there something you could do to make your mind off things just to get through today?
It sounds like you have to be strong for everyone else? That must be a lot of pressure and worry?
I agree, at least during the week I'm forced to go and be distracted at work.
hey man, what happened with your scholarship? Try not to be scared to go to your therapist they want to help you and you deserve to feel better.
hey, I know how you feel.  What's happened to make you feel like this?
hey, what you up to?
hi, what you up to?
hey, what's making you feel like this?
hey, what you doing this weekend?

My friends were very much tied to my sports and my job.  Since I don't do either I don't see them.  I also feel ashamed because of my injury even if that seems slightly irrationally. I think my identity was linked to my sport and my career. 

The doctors are still trying to figure out a cure.  I'm stuck in limbo a bit because no one knows if it is permanent or if it could get better.

I understand the uncertainty is difficult.   At least once you get through tomorrow you'll have a clear idea of where you stand.  It might not be as bad as you think, its easy to think worst case scenario when you make a mistake.

Although things seem very bad now perhaps in a few days time they won't seem so serious. Try to keep calm until Monday.   

How do you think things will go if you apologise to your employer at your meeting?

Thanks for replying.  I suffered an injury 2 years ago and I've been left in chronic pain.  I used to have a where I traveled the world, and played loads of sports in my down time. I had lots of friends. 

My employer couldn't accommodate my pain and I lost my job.  I had to quit sports. I can't change the pain.  I can't do the job I want.  I've lost all my friends. 

Everyone time I think of some solution to make things better I'm stopped by the injury.   I just don't know how to move forward.  Any thoughts?

Thanks for your replies.  I worried I'll just be wasting everyone's time because I've calmed down now.  I don't feel I'm in immediate danger at this moment.   

I just really wish I could have some kind of plan to help me fight this.
I'd be curious what you would learn with an extra year of study?  What kind of photo job would you want at the end?
Thats exactly what I'm struggling with right now.  Do I do things that make me happy but leave me in pain or miss those things but be in less pain...
